claim: Tracey Emin 'A Second Life' retrospective is at Tate Modern through 31 Aug 2026, alongside Julio Le Parc opening 11 June 2026 and Frida: The Making of an Icon from 25 June 2026.
quote: Tracey Emin: A Second Life... Until 31 Aug 2026. Julio Le Parc: 11 Jun 2026 – 3 May 2027. Frida: The Making of an Icon: 25 Jun 2026 – 4 Jan 2027.

claim: Time Out's top May/June 2026 picks include Tracey Emin at Tate Modern, James McNeill Whistler at Tate Britain (21 May–27 Sept), Zurbarán at the National Gallery (until 23 Aug), and Michaelina Wautier at the Royal Academy (until 21 June).
quote: James McNeill Whistler | Tate Britain... Until 27 Sept 2026... Zurbarán | The National Gallery... Until 23 Aug 2026... Michaelina Wautier | Royal Academy... Until 21 Jun 2026

claim: The National Gallery's headline late-spring show is Zurbarán (2 May – 23 August 2026), the first major UK monographic exhibition of the Spanish baroque master.
quote: Zurbarán (2 May – 23 August 2026) - The first major monographic exhibition in the UK devoted to Francisco de Zurbarán (1598–1664).

claim: The V&A's flagship paid show in spring 2026 is Schiaparelli: Fashion Becomes Art (opens 28 March, runs to 8 November 2026), the first major UK exhibition on the couture house with 200+ objects.
quote: Schiaparelli: Fashion Becomes Art... Opening March 28, 2026... runs until November 8, 2026... Over 200 objects will be on show

claim: The Design Museum's Wes Anderson: The Archives runs 21 November 2025 – 26 July 2026 with 700+ items including the Grand Budapest Hotel model and original costumes; booking advised.
quote: Wes Anderson: The Archives... runs from November 21, 2025 through July 26, 2026... more than 700 items including costumes, puppets, and original storyboards

claim: Wellcome Collection's free major show 'The Coming of Age' runs 26 March – 29 November 2026, with 120+ artworks and objects exploring perceptions of ageing.
quote: 'The Coming of Age' is a major exhibition... running from 26 March – 29 November 2026. The show brings together more than 120 artworks, objects and research projects

claim: Wallace Collection (free, Marylebone, open 7 days 10–17) runs 'Winston Churchill: The Painter' from 23 May–29 November 2026, the first major retrospective of his paintings since his death, gathering 50+ works.
quote: Winston Churchill: The Painter - This exhibition runs from 23 May–29 November 2026. The first major retrospective of Sir Winston Churchill's paintings since his death, this exhibition brings together more than 50 of his works.

claim: British Museum permanent collection is free; booking a free timed ticket in advance is recommended though walk-up entry is available, with longer waits possible at peak times.
quote: you're advised to book a free ticket in advance... walk-up visits are available each day for those who arrive at the Museum, without advance bookings... If visitor numbers are very high, non-ticket holders may have a longer wait

claim: Sir John Soane's Museum is free with no pre-booking, open Wednesday–Sunday 10–5 (closed Mon/Tue), so it's only viable for Wed-Sun weekend itineraries.
quote: The Museum is normally open Wednesday to Sunday, 10am to 5pm... The museum is closed Monday and Tuesday... Entry is free and there is no need to pre-book

claim: Churchill War Rooms costs £34 adult from 1 April 2026 (£29.70 concession, £16.50 child); booking ahead is recommended to pick a time slot and skip the queue, includes free multilingual audio guide.
quote: Adults cost from £33, though from 1 April 2026, adult tickets are £34. Seniors over 65, students, and travelers with disabilities pay £29.70, while children aged 5–15 are £16.50.

claim: V&A East Museum (new for 2026, Stratford) and V&A South Kensington's Rising Voices: Contemporary Art from Asia, Australia and the Pacific (from 16 May 2026) are notable additions to the V&A family this season.
quote: The V&A East Will Open This Weekend... Rising Voices: Contemporary Art from Asia, Australia and the Pacific... From May 16th, this exhibition brings work from 40 leading artists to South Kensington
